candidate_relations.reason: Rifampin-induced hemolysis is the upstream hemolytic event missing heme-pigment renal failure.
Rifampin-induced hemolytic anemia captures immune hemolysis (low haptoglobin, high LDH) but omits the pigment nephropathy.
Rifampin-induced nephritis implies interstitial inflammation, incompatible with hemoglobin-cast tubular injury on biopsy.
Rifampin-induced acute kidney injury is compatible but missing the required heme-pigment mechanism.
Acute tubular necrosis is the tubular injury pattern missing rifampin and heme pigment.
Hemoglobinuria is a laboratory component of pigment nephropathy, not the full diagnosis.
Rifampin-induced immune hemolytic anemia with hemoglobin-mediated acute tubular injury is the same heme-pigment renal-failure object.
Rhabdomyolysis is a related pigment nephropathy with incompatible myoglobin rather than hemoglobin casts.
Rifampin-induced acute renal failure due to heme pigment-related injury matches the reference diagnosis.
Rifampin-induced acute tubular necrosis omits the heme-pigment mechanism documented by hemoglobin IHC.
Tubulointerstitial nephritis is an incompatible inflammatory tubulointerstitial pattern.
Acute interstitial nephritis is the usual drug-kidney alternative, not hemoglobin-cast ATN.
Hemoglobinuric acute tubular necrosis is the renal lesion missing rifampin as the required cause.
Hemolytic-uremic syndrome is a TMA, not isolated heme-pigment ATN from rifampin hemolysis.
Rifampin-induced acute interstitial nephritis is an incompatible mechanism relative to heme-pigment injury.
Chronic kidney disease is not supported by a normal baseline creatinine of 0.96 mg/dL.
